stories.title: FAA traces nationwide ground stop to data flood on its telecom network; root cause still open
stories.location: United States (nationwide, FAA en route centers)
stories.alert_level: none (no GDACS-type alert for this event)
stories.summary: A flood of data on the Federal Aviation Administration's private telecommunications network forced Friday's nationwide ground stop, the FAA said, and every aircraft in the air landed safely. Air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. EST the same day. The root cause is still undetermined, Transportation Secretary Duffy said Monday. Microsoft's outage a day earlier was a separate event, according to Microsoft and Homeland Security Secretary Mullin.
stories.alert_note: Severity set by Journalist from scope (nationwide stop, thousands of cancellations); no external alert level exists.

confidence.conclusion: Microsoft is not linked to the FAA ground stop by any primary or official source; the two are separate outages.
The stop came from a data flood on the FAA's FTI telecom network, per the FAA; why the flood started (installer error, a faulty router or something else) is still under investigation.
No evidence links SMART to the stop, and the timing alone isn't evidence; the FAA, which denies a link, is the agency involved, so its denial is not independent.

canaries.indicator: FAA or L3Harris publishes a root-cause report separating installer error from a faulty router, and confirms or revises the Amarillo and El Dorado account
NTSB or DOT Inspector General announces an investigation or audit of the Nov 13 event
FBI or DOT discloses a finding on the El Dorado router, including whether tampering was ruled out

stories.title: Tropical Cyclone Wati intensifies near Suwarrow, with Aitutaki on alert
stories.location: Cook Islands: Northern Group near Suwarrow (RSMC Nadi storm centre 12.2S 163.5W at 162100Z, open water); forecast track toward Aitutaki, Southern Group
stories.summary: Tropical Cyclone Wati is strengthening as it moves southeast through the northern Cook Islands, with a cyclone warning in force for Suwarrow atoll and a cyclone alert for Aitutaki in the south.
stories.update_note: Updated with RSMC Nadi Northern Cooks bulletin #9 (162335Z): new 2100Z position and revised forecast pass south-southwest of Suwarrow.

stories.title: Champi strengthens into a typhoon as Guam braces for a close pass
stories.location: Guam and Northern Mariana Islands (storm centre approx. 12.0N 149.6E, open ocean)
stories.summary: Champi has strengthened into a typhoon over the western Pacific, and forecasters expect it to pass close to Guam this weekend as a strong typhoon.
stories.update_note: Champi upgraded to a typhoon in JTWC warning 10; GDACS alert raised to Red; Coastal Flood Watch upgraded to Warning; added hospital, port and shelter preparations and rainfall forecast.

stories.title: Satellite monitors flag low-impact forest fires in Botswana and Mozambique
stories.summary: A global disaster-alert system has recorded four forest fires in southern Africa this month: one in northern Botswana and three in central Mozambique. The system rated all four at its lowest alert level.
stories.location: Chobe District, Botswana; Zambezia province, Mozambique
stories.update_note: Adds GDACS 1032672 (32,246 ha, Zambezia) and GDACS people-in-burned-area counts; limits burning-season context to Botswana.

stories.title: Indonesia battles worst forest fires in over a decade as haze spreads across region
stories.alert_level: GDACS Green (lowest) for all four mapped events
stories.summary: Indonesia is fighting its worst forest and land fires in more than a decade, The Independent reported Friday. Four members of a firefighting team died, and the government has agreed to accept foreign help.
stories.location: Indonesia (national; GDACS events in South Sumatra, West Papua, South Papua, North Maluku)

stories.title: Deep magnitude 5.9 earthquake strikes Fiji region, no tsunami threat
stories.summary: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck deep beneath the sea in the Fiji region at 10:49 GMT on Oct. 14, the U.S. Geological Survey reported.

stories.title: Satellite alert flags low-impact wildfire in northeastern Nigeria
stories.summary: A wildfire burned about 7,464 hectares, roughly 18,400 acres, in far northeastern Nigeria from Oct. 7 to Oct. 14, according to the Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System.

stories.title: Flash flooding in Tripoli kills at least one, prompts investigation
stories.summary: Torrential rain flooded Libya's capital, Tripoli, on Tuesday, killing at least one person, the Libya Herald reported. Some reports put the death toll at two.

stories.title: Tropical Storm Simon weakens off Mexico's Baja California coast
stories.summary: Tropical Storm Simon is weakening over open water south of Mexico's Baja California peninsula, and forecasters expect it to fall apart this weekend, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said Friday.
